text:
Maria Nguyen: quick sync — Veridian private deploy is hitting two last-mile blockers: KMS key policy not accepting RBAC from their CI role, and our egress rule to their log-collector is still failing. any quick wins?

Devon Patel: on it. saw the KMS error earlier: "NotAuthorizedException: access denied for kms:Decrypt" when their deploy runs. likely key policy + account principal mismatch.

Aisha Gomez: fwiw their infra team handed over a cross-account role arn: arn:aws:iam::765432109876:role/veridian-deploy-role — did they add the key policy statement with that exact ARN? common mismatch is using a wildcard or external id missing.

Samir Rao: Maria — can you paste the key policy they provided? I can validate quickly.

Maria Nguyen: pasted below (from their ticket):

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "Allow use from Veridian deploy",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::765432109876:role/veridian-deploy-role"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```

Devon Patel: that looks fine at first glance. two checks: 1) the KMS is a multi-account key? if it's in our acct, principal must be the veridian role ARN and the policy must also allow kms:DescribeKey for cross-account usage sometimes. 2) confirm the deploy is using the same role ARN (no session name swapping).

Aisha Gomez: also need to verify they didn't attach a condition like "StringEquals": {"kms:ViaService": "ec2.amazonaws.com"} — that would block CI.

Samir Rao: quick IAM command they can run to validate the role identity during the build: 

```
aws sts get-caller-identity --query Arn
```

Maria Nguyen: I asked them to run that and forward output. meanwhile the egress issue: infra-bot shows connection resets to their log endpoint 10.11.45.22:443 from our NAT gateway.

Devon Patel: they use a Splunk HEC endpoint with client certs, right? are we NATting but not allowing the outbound TLS SNI? odd. show their endpoint DNS?

Maria Nguyen: their ticket lists logs.veridian-prod.splk.example.com -> 10.11.45.22

Aisha Gomez: recommend they test from a bastion in their VPC to prove connectivity. if name resolves to private IP, confirm peering or transit config. also check SG egress rule on our side allows ports 443/ TLS.

Samir Rao: small ops-runbook note: when customers use private deployments we should ask for: 1) KMS key policy with exact role ARN, 2) egress CIDR + DNS names, 3) example curl from their network to our webhook and vice-versa. saves this back-and-forth. can we add that to the onboarding checklist?

Maria Nguyen: yes please. adding follow-up item to handoff doc.

infra-bot: Reminder: runbook snippet deployed at https://redwood.internal/runbooks/private-onboard — updated 2026-03-20 09:04 UTC

Devon Patel: I validated their key policy in a sandbox: it's allowed but their role has a trust policy that only allows sts:AssumeRole from a specific AWS account alias, looks like the deploy tries to assume from a session not matching the condition. I'll ask them for the exact assume role call logs.

Maria Nguyen: pinged Veridian infra (cc @veridian-ops) to get get-caller-identity output and their deploy assumeRole logs. they replied they'll share within 30 mins. :thumbsup:

Aisha Gomez: once we get the sts output, I can craft the minimal key-policy patch and they can apply. then we re-run deploy smoke.

Samir Rao: also flagged potential renewal risk: this customer's onboarding is +2 days beyond SLA window; if we don't get cutover in next 48h mark we should escalate to AM. I'll open a short ticket after today if we remain blocked.

Maria Nguyen: noted. I'll keep this thread updated. thanks all.

Devon Patel: follow-up: if they need temporary access we can create a short-lived key alias for onboarding testing (audit will need aware) — Aisha ok with that?

Aisha Gomez: fine with temporary alias, but must be scoped and logged. ask them to sign the access window in the ticket.

Maria Nguyen: update 20m later — Veridian ran get-caller-identity, it's arn:aws:sts::765432109876:assumed-role/veridian-deploy-role/ci-session-42. they also attached the assumeRole audit which shows ExternalId: null.

Devon Patel: that matches my suspicion. need their key policy to allow the assumed-role ARN pattern or the role principal (use the role ARN, not the assumed session). sample snippet to add: 

```
{"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::765432109876:role/veridian-deploy-role"},"Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"]}
```

Maria Nguyen: I pushed that suggestion to their ticket. they're applying now.

infra-bot: Audit note: ticket #CS-4827 updated by Maria Nguyen — KMS policy suggestion added.

Samir Rao: once KMS is green, I'll re-check egress flow. if still failing we can do a short ssh into our NAT and tcpdump to capture TLS handshake.

Maria Nguyen: excellent. closing loop for now — will update when they confirm. thanks all.
